observed_failure.why: Stored constraints are unscoped strings and fast-path readiness does not test whether they make the current milestone or next action impossible.
observed_failure.reproduction: A valid verified schema-version-3 checkpoint whose next action edits app.py and whose permission_constraints forbids editing app.py still returns fast_path_ready=true.

rejected_replay_boundary: Do not add a self-attested decision artifact without binding it to current checkpoint intent, and do not retry a prose-only intent classifier that lacks deterministic stale-state invalidation.

candidate.cause: Constraint authority, applicability, and review freshness are not represented in the live checkpoint.
candidate.mechanism: Store only active typed constraints with event-scoped applicability and revisit conditions, require imported strings to be classified, bind one compatible/blocked/unknown review to current checkpoint intent, fail fast on conflicts, and permit no second workaround for the same unresolved constraint.
candidate.prediction: The candidate will block real permission and ambiguous project conflicts before execution, ignore a constraint from another milestone, preserve compatible constraints, and honor an exact current-user supersession without broadening permissions.
candidate.falsification_condition: Reject when any conflict case executes, any compatible case blocks, an obsolete milestone constraint remains applicable, an exact override broadens beyond its stated scope, a changed checkpoint reuses an old compatible review, or legacy state enters fast resume without migration and re-verification.
candidate.rollback: Restore the 2.2.1 skill and schema-version-3 checkpoint behavior; keep the failed evidence and do not bump the plugin version.

evaluation.primary_metric: exact constraint decisions without execution-time workarounds
guardrails: no false block on compatible work
evaluation.comparison: Same-model champion/candidate paired A/B in four counterbalanced rounds plus deterministic negative controls.

refinement_rule: Only one distinct refinement may replace the first candidate, and only when deterministic or paired evidence identifies a concrete false block, missed conflict, stale-review gap, or material cost regression.
claim_boundary: DEV and VALIDATION evidence for a local 2.3.0 candidate only. No HOLDOUT, personal, broad cross-project, public-release, or universal runtime claim is preregistered.
